filesystem.description: Broad filesystem read/write access rooted at /home/mateo - per the user's explicit broad-access choice. This also covers the synced Kearney & O'Banion Dropbox folder for free (no separate Dropbox integration needed). Via @modelcontextprotocol/server-filesystem (npx-launched Node MCP server, stdio transport). Same y/n-per-call confirmation model as every other tool in llmcli.py --tools - broad capability, not blind autonomy.
notes: command is the node22 binary directly (not bare 'npx') running npx-cli.js as a script - this bypasses npx's own '#!/usr/bin/env node' shebang, which would otherwise re-resolve 'node' via PATH and silently find system Node 12 (EOL, apt) again, dying with 'SyntaxError: Unexpected reserved word'. This is the exact invocation verified end-to-end by cli/mcp_smoke_test.py. llmcli.py's loader also injects node22/bin at the front of PATH for every configured server as a second layer of defense, for anything a server spawns internally.

playwright.description: Unrestricted headless browser automation (navigate, click, type, screenshot, evaluate JS, etc.) - per the user's explicit broad-access choice, not locked to specific sites. Via @playwright/mcp (Microsoft's official Playwright MCP server - @modelcontextprotocol/server-puppeteer is dead/deprecated, do not use it). --isolated keeps the browser profile in-memory only (no persistent user-data-dir). --executable-path points at the system's installed google-chrome so this server doesn't try to download its own Chromium. Same y/n-per-call confirmation model as every other tool in llmcli.py --tools.
notes: Same node22-direct-invocation pattern as the filesystem entry above, for the same reason.

This server's tool schema alone is ~24 tools / ~17.7KB (roughly 4400 tokens by a bytes/4 estimate). Combined with filesystem's ~14 tools, the merged schema measured ~6637 prompt tokens against a live qwen-next server. Re-enabled 2026-08-25 by raising qwen-next's GPU_CTX from 4096 to 8192 in bin/start-model.sh (see that file's qwen-next case) to fit the merged schema plus real conversation headroom. llmcli.py prints a startup warning if the merged schema looks too large for the connected model's actual context size (queried live from /slots). If you hit 'exceeds context size' errors again (e.g. running scout, which is still at a smaller GPU_CTX), disable one server here rather than running both against a small-context model, or raise that model's GPU_CTX/CTX if you have the VRAM/RAM to spare.

google-drive.description: Google Drive + Docs + Sheets + Slides + Calendar, via @piotr-agier/google-drive-mcp (npx-launched Node MCP server, stdio transport). Same y/n-per-call confirmation model as read_file/run_shell in llmcli.py --tools - broad capability, not blind autonomy.
notes: System Node (/usr/bin/node) on this machine is v12 (EOL, apt) and cannot run this server - it uses ES2022 top-level await and dies with 'SyntaxError: Unexpected reserved word'. A modern Node 22 LTS is already downloaded standalone (no sudo) to /home/mateo/local-llm/.tools/node22/. Whatever launches this 'npx' command (this client, or the user running the auth command by hand) needs that node22/bin ahead of system node on PATH. See cli/mcp_smoke_test.py for the exact, already-proven-working invocation pattern (it hardcodes the node22 paths and explains why 'env node' re-resolution defeats a naive fix) - reuse that pattern here rather than re-deriving it.

The token cache (tokens.json) is left at the server's own default (~/.config/google-drive-mcp/tokens.json), outside this repo - only the OAuth client credentials file lives at credentialsPath above, and only that path needs to be gitignored.
